title: Introduction to Human Geography
description: (GEOG 1302) Introduction to Human Geography. This course introduces students to fundamental concepts, skills and practices of human geography. Place, space and scale serve as a framework for understanding patterns of human experience. Topics for discussion may include globalization, population and migration, culture, diffusion, political and economic systems, language, religion, gender and ethnicity; also taught at Galveston campus.

title: Geography of the Global Village
description: (GEOG 1303) Geography of the Global Village. Survey of world regions; globalization; environmental problems at multiple scales; human-environment interactions; cultural coherence and diversity; population and settlement; geopolitics; social and economic development; place identification; also taught at Galveston campus.

title: Planet Earth
description: (GEOG 1301) Planet Earth. Earth’s physical environment including climate, water, landforms, and ecosystems; processes that control these systems and their global distributions; human effects on these processes.

title: Environmental Change
description: Systems perspective on important attributes, elements, and connections within earth's physical environment; dynamic nature of environment at multiple spatial and temporal scales.

title: Planet Earth Lab
description: Exercises and maps to illustrate principles of physical geography.

title: Geospatial Cornerstone
description: Professional career options, methods, strategies and skills involved in successful career planning in the geospatial sciences; highlights high impact learning opportunities such as study abroad and internships and the development of scientific communication skills.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: GEOG and GIST majors; sophomore classification or approval of instructor.

title: Cartography and Visualization
description: Introduction to science and art of map production; principles of thematic map compilation and design; history of thematic mapping; map projections; data management and symbolization; common types and styles of thematic maps.

title: Directed Studies
description: Individually-supervised research or intensive study on topics not covered in regular courses.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Approval of department head.

title: Special Topics In...
description: Selected topics in an identified area of geography. May be repeated for credit.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: GEOG, GIST or USGE majors, or approval of instructor.

title: Research
description: Research conducted under the direction of faculty member in geography. May be taken 2 times for credit. Registration in multiple sections of this course is possible within a given semester provided that the per semester credit hour limit is not exceeded.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Freshman or sophomore classification and approval of instructor.
repeatability: May be taken 2 times for credit.

title: Geography of the United States
description: This systematic and regional course introduces geographic issues covering the geography of the United States from environmental, political, social/cultural and economic perspectives with a focus on the many ways that culture, politics, economics and social difference are manifested in and through spatial relations and processes. Our case studies will emphasize that the United States is an ever-changing configuration of ideas, institutions, people and objects. This course also aims to develop conceptual tools for critical thinking, rather than an encyclopedic knowledge of the United States’ geographic features. Finally, the course introduces students to a variety of concepts and methods that geographers use to analyze spatial patterns and processes.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Junior or senior classification; also taught at Galveston campus.

title: Health Geography
description: Overview of health-related issues within society, including diseases, healthcare services, access to healthcare, environmental health, food and nutrition, urban health, neighborhood health, climate and health using geographical approaches.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Junior or senior classification.

title: Economic Geography
description: Location of economic activities over the earth; distribution of agriculture, manufacturing, tertiary activities and transportation; economic growth of areas.

title: Geography of Texas
description: Exploration into the geographic personality of Texas: past and current physical and biotic environments; cultural pluralism, including ethnic origins and distinctive human ecologies; and the social, economic and political sources of environmental problems.

title: Introduction to Urban Geography
description: Reasons humankind tends to congregate in cities. Overview of patterns in the geographic distribution of cities, and in the geographic distribution of peoples and activities within cities, and the dynamics of these distributions.

title: Geography of Energy
description: Development of high-energy society; renewable and nonrenewable energy resources and systems; physical and social economies of energy use; geography of energy systems; energy problems and decisions; energy governance; dependence of other resources on energy; decarbonization policies and scenarios; alternative energy futures.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Junior classification or approval of instructor.

title: Cultural Geography
description: Human factors which affect man-land relationship; concept of culture, culture areas; population growth and migrations, types of economic activity, urban and transportation geography.

title: Data Analysis in Geography
description: Foundation for collection and analysis of quantitative and qualitative geographic data; emphasis on hands-on, practical experience with commonly used analysis software and qualitative methods including interviewing and archival research; problems commonly encountered in dealing with data.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: STAT 303 .

title: The Middle East
description: Regional geography of the Middle East; physical setting and the historical evolution of Middle Eastern landscapes; current issues.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Junior or senior classification.

title: Geography of Latin America
description: Physical and cultural characteristics of Latin America; physical landscape, cultural succession and the present cultural landscape; details on sub-regions.

title: Global Climatic Regions
description: Climatological processes and their consequences for spatial distributions of climates; survey of earth's climates; relationships among climate, landforms, vegetation, soils and humans.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: GEOG 203 or ATMO 201 or approval of instructor.

title: Geography of Europe
description: Regional geography of European landmass; global, political and cultural characteristics of European geography in historical and ecological contexts.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Junior or senior classification.

title: Resources and the Environment
description: Changing demand for land and sea resources; international conditions of population growth, resource depletion and geopolitical control; resource perceptions and decision-making.

title: Geomorphology
description: Processes and principles of landscape evolution across Earth’s surface environments; laboratory in landscape evolution, sediment analysis, and field observation.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: GEOL 101 or GEOG 203 ; also taught at Galveston campus.

title: Pattern and Process in Biogeography
description: Distribution of organisms across the earth and on environmental and cultural processes that have contributed to these patterns of distribution; dynamic nature of biogeographic patterns; impacts of contemporary and prehistoric humans on plant and animal distributions; methods for exploring biogeographic patterns and detecting change.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Junior or senior classification.

title: GNSS in the Geosciences
description: Fundamentals of Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS); basic geodesy, figure of the earth; frames of reference, map projection, datums, ellipsoids; GPS accuracy and precision; applications in earth resource mapping and database creation; elementary GPS phase data processing.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Junior or senior classification or approval of instructor. Cross Listing: GEOL 352/GEOG 352 .

title: Natural Hazards
description: Introduction to the types and causes of natural events that pose risk to society; an examination of prevailing concepts and theories of human response and vulnerability; characteristics of natural events; natural hazard paradigms; case studies.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: GEOG 203 or GEOL 101 ; junior or senior classification; also taught at Galveston campus.

title: Remote Sensing in Geosciences
description: Introduction to the principles, techniques and applications of remote sensing technology in geosciences including the analysis and interpretation of airborne and spaceborne remote sensing data for studying key earth system processes.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Junior or senior classification.

title: Coastal Processes
description: Introduction to the coastal system, waves and wave dominated coasts, shoreline morphodynamics, tidal and lake coasts, long term coastal development, sea level changes, subtidal and beach ecosystems, coastal dunes and wetlands, structures and organizations, coastal management and coastal hazards.
prerequisites: Cross Listing: MARS 370/GEOG 370 .

title: Workshop in Environmental Studies
description: The study, understanding and solution of human environment problems based on principles learned in the classroom; library, laboratory and field work carried out by individuals and in groups; reports on work accomplished. May be taken three times for credit.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: GEOG 330 .
repeatability: May be taken three times for credit.

title: Principles of Geographic Information Systems
description: Basic concepts of design, planning and implementation of geographic information systems.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Junior or senior classification.

title: Geodatabases
description: GIS data modeling; introductory and advanced spatial SQL (structured query language); spatial database management system (DBMS) server setup, management and maintenance; spatial DBMS design, implementation, tuning, performance analysis and indexing; connecting spatial data services and warehouses to GIS software.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Junior or senior classification.

title: GIS Programming
description: Programming for geographic information science applications; principles of programming syntax and data structures; development of custom GIS programs; integration of programs into commercial GIS platforms.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: GEOG 390 or equivalent, or approval of instructor; junior or senior classification.

title: Cartography and Geovisualization
description: Cartographic and data visualization applications of Geographic Information Systems (GIS); theory and practice of cartographic decisions and design; user interface, map design, and visualization of geospatial, spatiotemporal, 3D, and big data; designed map experiences for different environments and purposes.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: GEOG 390 .

title: Aerial Imagery Analysis and Geospatial Machine Learning
description: Identification and evaluation of natural and cultural features on aerial images; methods for extracting information concerning land use, vegetative cover, surface and structural features, urban/industrial patterns and archaeological sites; image-based geospatial machine learning techniques.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: GEOG 361 and GEOG 390 ; junior or senior classification, or approval of instructor.

title: Arid Lands Geomorphology
description: Introduction to the geomorphology of deserts; processes, origin and evolution of arid lands; urban geomorphology in drylands; desertification.

title: Political Geography
description: The political process at a variety of geographic scales: international, intranational and urban; origins of territorial organization and conflicts over access to and use of space and its resources.

title: Field Trips
description: Supervised field trip to investigate the physical, economic and cultural processes that influence the spatial development and distribution on the landscape. May be repeated for credit.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: GEOG 201 , GEOG 202 , GEOG 203 or GEOG 205 , or concurrent enrollment; approval of instructor.

title: Geographic Perspectives on Contemporary Urban Issues
description: Contemporary readings on spatial patterns and processes in urban environments; sprawl; human-environment interaction; housing; development and growth; concept of place; scale; power and policy.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: GEOG 304 or GEOG 306 or equivalent.

title: Geographies of Decarbonization
description: Geographical analysis of decarbonizing energy systems; territorialization and justice processes associated with decarbonization; implications of decarbonization for places and landscapes; influence of path dependencies and institutions on decarbonization.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: GEOG 330 or GEOG 309 or approval of instructor.

title: Global Change
description: The interaction of the earth, atmosphere, oceans, cryosphere and life, including the impact of human society on the environment and climate; global change modeling; politics, policy and decision making; and personal awareness.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Junior or senior classification. Cross Listing: OCNG 412/GEOG 410 .

title: Geography of Terrorism
description: Exploration of global terrorism and counter terrorism; regional conflicts and mass violence; construction of places and regions associated with terror; American reactions to global terrorism.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Junior or senior classification.

title: Environmental Justice
description: This course examines the uneven distribution of environmental benefits and burdens across society, drawing on the scholarly literature referred to as environmental justice research. You will examine historical and contemporary evidence for disparities in exposure to environmental hazards, including but not limited to air and water pollution, as well as disparities in access to environmental amenities, including but not limited to urban greenspace. Topics address variation in environmental conditions and policy outcomes across different demographic and geographic contexts, including those associated with race, gender, ethnicity and class, as these social categories are used in empirical research and policy analysis. The course treats these social categories as analytical descriptors rather than normative or ideological claims. Content includes controversial and contested scholarly perspectives on environmental issues, reflecting multiple explanatory frameworks for understanding the causes of and proposed policy responses to uneven environmental distributions. Drawing on readings from a range of disciplines, such as environmental science, geography and urban planning, you will evaluate proposed explanations for observed patterns, including but not limited to market dynamics, land-use decisions, regulatory enforcement, historical settlement patterns and institutional decision-making processes. You will also compare policy and governance responses discussed in the scholarly literature, such as market-based mechanisms, participatory decision-making arrangements and strengthened regulatory oversight, assessing their assumptions, empirical support and trade-offs. The course emphasizes evidence-based reasoning and civil discourse, preparing you to engage constructively with contentious environmental policy contexts. An independent research project will train you to develop and defend an analytical argument related to an environmental justice issue of your choosing using appropriate evidence. Throughout the course, your work will be evaluated on the quality of analysis and reasoning, not on agreement with any particular political, moral or ideological position.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: GEOG 201 or GEOG 202 ; junior or senior classification.

title: Hydrology and Environment
description: Examination of hydrologic processes in relation to climate, soils, vegetation, land use practices, and human impacts; natural scientific perspectives emphasized; field and laboratory included.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: GEOG 203 or equivalent.

title: Principles of Plant Geography
description: Plant distributions, their associations and environmental relationships; survey of the principal explanatory systems; field and laboratory study of area patterns at various geographic scales. A weekend field trip is required.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: BIOL 101 or BIOL 107 or BIOL 301 or approval of instructor.

title: History and Nature of Geography
description: Summary of classical knowledge of world; development of thought on nature of geography from 1800 to present.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Junior or senior classification.

title: Past Climates
description: Terrestrial and marine proxy records of past climate variability, including tree rings, coral, and sediments; past climate change events such as the Little Ice Age and Medieval Warm Period; greenhouse gases and global temperature; insight into the nature of climate change and challenges humankind faces in the next few centuries.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: GEOL 101 , GEOL 104 , GEOL 150 , ATMO 201 , GEOG 203 , or OCNG 251 ; junior or senior classification. Cross Listing: GEOL 442/GEOG 442 .

title: Global Biogeochemical Cycles
description: Use of biogeochemical cycles to study the Earth system; description of movement and transformation of major elements such as C, N, P and trace elements; flux of material in and out of atmosphere, hydrosphere, pedosphere, and lithosphere; chemical and physical transformations that occur in Earth system.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: CHEM 119 and CHEM 120 ; select two from ATMO 201 , or OCNG 251 , or GEOG 203 or GEOG 205 , or GEOL 101 or GEOL 104 or GEOL 150 . Cross Listing: GEOL 443/GEOG 443 .

title: Field Geography
description: Introduction to field methods; documenting materials, reconnaissance, the field plan; mapping traverse, base maps and aerial photographs; recording techniques; interview procedures. Fields trips required, some on weekends and/or semester breaks, for which departmental fees may be assessed to cover costs.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: 15 hours of geography or equivalent.

title: Urban Climatology and Human Biometeorology
description: Comprehensive examination of urban climates and human well-being, with an exploration of urban atmospheric processes, thermal comfort and health impacts; foundational concepts in biometeorology and nature-based solutions are evaluated based on fieldwork, data analysis and applied projects.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Junior or senior classification.

title: Digital Image Processing in the Geosciences
description: Key remote-sensing digital image processing methods; advanced topics in feature extraction, radiometric calibration, image enhancement, pattern recognition and geoscience applications.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: GEOG 361 or equivalent and junior or senior classification.

title: Advanced GIS Analysis for Natural Resources Management
description: Advanced topics in geographic information systems (GIS) to solve natural resource problems; manipulation of raster data types; three-dimensional modeling; emphasis on geoprocessing as it relates to applied projects particularly with habitat suitability models; field and lab use of global positioning systems (GPS); internet-based GIS modeling.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: ECCB 351 , RWFM 351 , or AGSM 461 , or equivalent, or approval of instructor; junior or senior classification. Cross Listing: ECCB 406/GEOG 462 .

title: Dynamic Modeling of Earth and Environmental Systems
description: Dynamical systems modeling; key concepts and processes in earth and environmental systems; human impact on these systems; model building and testing; system behavior over time; model validation and sensitivity; examples from the applications in earth and environmental sciences.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: GEOG 203 or approval of instructor.

title: Drones for Geographic Analysis and Applications
description: Current topics in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAVs, also known as drone) operations and their use in geographic information science and technology (GIST); legal and professional certification requirements; laws and regulations of drone-based data collection; platform and payload selection; safe flight planning and operations; data collection and processing; end-product creation, visualization and analysis; and preparation for the FAA Remote Pilot Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Part 107 Certification Exam.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: GEOG 390 ; junior or senior classification, or approval of instructor.

title: Advanced Topics in GIS (Geographic Information Systems)
description: Advanced Topics in Geographic Information Systems. Topics related to GIS implementation, spatial database design, spatial data analysis, and various advanced GIS applications.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: GEOG 390 or equivalent.

title: GIS Practicum
description: Introduction to current topics in Geographic Information Science including ethical and legal issues surrounding spatial technologies, proper GIS management practices and professional certification; development of professional research, technical and communication skills through participation in a coordinated internship or independent research project. Meets writing-intensive course requirements for environmental geosciences, environmental studies and geography majors.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Senior classification and enrollment in Geographic Information Science and Technology or approval of instructor.

title: Terrain Analysis and Mapping
description: Geomorphometry for land surface characterization; fundamentals of terrain analysis; theory of land surface dynamics; application of software for digital terrain modeling and analysis.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: GEOG 361 and GEOG 390 or equivalents, or approval of instructor; junior or senior classification.

title: WebGIS
description: Investigation of web-based geographic information systems; introduction to server-oriented architectures for web-based applications and services; development of web applications; management of web servers, web services and databases.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: GEOG 390 or equivalent, or approval of instructor; junior or senior classification.

title: Principles of Geocomputation
description: Geocomputation including geospatial technologies, computational techniques and algorithms utilizing high-performance computing; fundamental geocomputation principles, artificial and computational intelligence.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: GEOG 361 , GEOG 390 , GEOG 475 ; CSCE 110 or CSCE 111 .

title: Internship
description: Directed internship in a private firm, government agency or non-governmental organization to provide work experience related to the student's degree program and career objectives.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Junior or senior classification and approval of internship agency and departmental internship director.

prerequisites: Prerequisite: Approval of department head.
